subject.title: Session lane starvation: followup drain monopolizes session lane, blocks inbound dispatch for 20-30min

question: What scheduler invariant should OpenClaw use when fresh user/control work arrives while same-session background or follow-up work is queued or running?
rationale: The bug is source-backed, but the durable fix requires choosing between foreground preemption, bounded drain fairness, and preserving current follow-up ordering semantics; code alone cannot pick that product/safety tradeoff.

options.title: Foreground-over-background scheduler
options.body: Make fresh user/control work overtake or abort/defer background follow-up work while preserving serialization and ordering inside each priority class.

options.title: Bounded follow-up drain
options.body: Cap consecutive follow-up turns or elapsed drain time before yielding, which reduces starvation but may not fully fix stop/control semantics during active background work.

options.title: Keep current queue semantics
options.body: Document and rely on existing followup/collect waiting behavior plus diagnostics/recovery, accepting that foreground messages can remain delayed behind backlogs.

recommendation.title: Foreground-over-background scheduler
recommendation.body: Make fresh user/control work overtake or abort/defer background follow-up work while preserving serialization and ordering inside each priority class.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the most recent adjacent foreground-delivery and current-main queue/drain changes and is the best available routing candidate for the scheduler-policy decision.
